newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sony to unveil digital broadcast equipment in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Sony to unveil digital broadcast equipment in U.S..

text.p: Sony Corp said it would unveil at a news conference in New York on Wednesday a new line of studio-use broadcasting equipment that can produce digital high-definition programming.
A Sony spokeswoman said it will be the first such product introduced in the United States since the U.S. government came up with an industry-wide standard for digital broadcasts late last year.
Sony's equipment will be shown at a broadcasting equipment fair, the National Association of Broadcasters, which begins in Las Vegas on April 7, the spokeswoman said.

Sony declined to give any details of the new products, but Wednesday's edition of the New York Times said that they would include high-definition cameras for use in studios, portable cameras for mobile news crews and a line of high-definition studio monitors.
Some of the equipment will be available as early as this spring, the report said, adding that the equipment would cost about 30 percent more than equivalent products now available.

The U.S. government plans to temporarily assign each of the nation's 1,600 television stations a second channel for digital high-definition television broadcasts that will let them change from the current analog technology to all-digital broadcasting during the next decade, the paper said.
Stations will have to replace nearly all their production and transmission equipment in the coming years so they can broadcast the new programming, it said.
